finding.summary: Phase 1 measured the RAW separated vocals, not the de-reverbed ones.
finding.mechanism: analysis/aeq/corpus.py build_manifest(): files are split on '(Reverb)'. Anything else is taken as the dry file, and the model tag is parsed from '(Mel-Roformer...)' or '(BS-RoFormer...)'. The raw vocals are named '(Vocals) (Mel-Roformer deux by becruily).mp3' with no (Dry) tag, so they were treated as dry.
finding.consequence: Every number in analysis/out/*.json describes raw separated vocals carrying the original reverb. The (Dry) stems were never measured.
finding.why_it_matters: It is not an error - the raw vocals are internally consistent, all 13 measured the same way. But it means the corpus baseline has reverb energy in it, and any new set must be measured the SAME way to be comparable.
finding.opportunity: Proper (Dry) stems exist for all 13. Measuring everything on (Dry) - old and new - would remove the de-reverb artefact question entirely, because then the de-reverb is applied to every song by the same tool.
finding.recommendation: Keep using the raw vocals for the archived 13 numbers (they cannot be recomputed without re-downloading), UNLESS the audio is re-placed in the workspace, in which case re-run the corpus on (Dry) and compare: the delta dry-minus-raw is the calibration curve.

naming_convention_required_for_new_files: <song title> - <artist> (Vocals) (Mel-Roformer deux by becruily) (Dry) (BS-RoFormer by playdasegunda).mp3
